summary: F2 relaxation (-1 in span of prime-factor classes mod squares) was tested for all 57,450 (p<6000 with p≡1(4), C≤150) pairs: it is necessary (0 wins without it) but holds in 16,736 pairs of which only 1,522 win (9.1%), so the linear layer is far from sufficient. The genus-layer lemma itself is already in the repo (Z52_BANKED genus layer).
Lit check: 'Gaussian almost primes in almost all narrow sectors' (Hecke Größencharakter): almost-all sector results only. No pointwise or ES quantity.
Divisor-interval and AP bounds for d | 4Cp+1 are the divisor-class analysis in EXSET_SHIFT_DIVISORS.md.
The comparison of observed δ(X) with the independent product is in BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md (independence prediction at X = 1000, l.44–60).
R(p) = #{m ≡3 mod 4 : r_p(m) | (m+1)/4} is already verified for p<=1009 in z52b_free_opus.md (item 266; scripts/z52b_free_opus_check1.py).

Increasing-denominator convention (x≤y≤z) gives median count U=62 over primes ≤5000; 50.7% of primes have a solution with two equal denominators (isosceles law, Z0973). Ordered-count recomputation not needed for the convention question.
R_100(3681=9*409)=14, R_100(10225=25*409)=6: not in the exceptional set at K=100. 3*409 is 3 mod 4 (outside the family).
Meta/organisational: exporting the FRONTIER barrier map as a CSV and web page is a repo-organisation task, not a test of an ES approach.

Reproduced the Carmichael-richness ratio on 10 Carmichael numbers ≤ 3·10⁴ (median U(n)/median of 1-mod-4 neighbours within ±6 = 3.8, range 0.54–7.75). No repo memo covers Carmichael numbers in the ES count. The compounding test (semiprimes pq with both p, q hard) was not run; the sample is too small to add a claim.

Log-geometry boundary of ES charts reduces to the coordinate divisor {xyz=0}, whose transform under birational charts carries no arithmetic beyond the equation itself. No ES-specific test follows, so this is a restatement.
Restatement: the CRT least positive representative is definitional, and the item gives no cost function beyond that representative.
